title: Technological Determinism
body:
**Technological determinism** holds that technology develops according to its own internal
logic and that society adapts to whatever arrives. On this view the printing press caused the
Reformation, the mechanical clock caused industrial work discipline, and the mobile phone
caused the change in how people arrange to meet.

Its appeal is that it explains large historical shifts economically, and it matches how
technological change feels from inside: nobody voted for the smartphone and everybody
rearranged their life around it.

Its weakness is that it treats the technology as though nobody chose it. Somebody decided which
features to build, which to fund and which to market, and those decisions had authors with
interests. Determinism removes them from the account, which also removes anyone who could be
held responsible.

[[Social Construction of Technology]] is the opposing position, and the two mark
the ends of a continuum. Placing a specific technology on it is the exercise, and for most the
honest answer sits in the middle: the capability constrains what is possible and social choice
decides which possibility gets built.
